\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Low Degree}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.Applications.LowDegree
\section{Overview}
Bounded-degree functions on finite probability products satisfy higher-moment estimates, sharp first-to-second norm comparison, one-sided anticoncentration, and optimized tail bounds. All estimates allow different full-support laws in different coordinates.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Second norm noise contraction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_noise_norm_two_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_noise}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $0\le c\le1$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\|T_cf\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

Then $\|T_cf\|_{2,P}\le c^k\|f\|_{2,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; degree at most $k$ means $h_S=0$ for every $|S|>k$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Higher norms of bounded-degree functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_lowDegree_norm}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.HasDegreeLE, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_lowDegree_noise_norm_two, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_noise_inverse}

Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $\lambda$, where $0<\lambda\le1$, and let $q>2$. For $k\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ of degree at most $k$, $\|f\|_{q,P}\le(\sqrt{q-1}\lambda^{1/q-1/2})^k\|f\|_{2,P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; degree at most $k$ means $h_S=0$ for every $|S|>k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Explicit comparison constant bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant}
\difficulty{5}
For every $0<\lambda\le1/2$, define $C_\lambda=\begin{cases}e,&\lambda=1/2,\\((1-\lambda)/\lambda)^{1/(2(1-2\lambda))},&\lambda\ne1/2.\end{cases}$. Then $C_\lambda\le e/\sqrt{2\lambda}$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_oneSided_anticoncentration}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.anticoncentration_coarse_lower_bound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.ComparisonAux.centered_probability_ge_of_norm_comparison, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.HasDegreeLE, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.variance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.degree_pos_of_variance_pos, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.hasDegreeLE_sub_const, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.productNormComparisonConstant_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_lowDegree_l1_l2}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1/2$. If $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ has degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$ and positive variance, then $\tfrac14(e^2/(2\lambda))^{-k}\le\Pr_P(\mathbb E_Pf<f)$ and $(15/\lambda)^{-k}\le\tfrac14(e^2/(2\lambda))^{-k}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\operatorname{Var}_P(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-\mathbb E_Ph)^2$; $\Pr_P(A)=\mathbb E_P\mathbf1_A$, where $\mathbf1_A$ is $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere; degree at most $k$ means $h_S=0$ for every $|S|>k$.
\end{theorem}
